relevance_note: Reports three families with GFAP variants and Alexander disease, e.g. 'Family A contains four siblings in whom we found a novel p.Ser247Pro mutation that was paternally inherited.'
method_note: Read in full; output built with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans (no table transcription; the paper has no data tables). Scope: Family A (I.a, I.b, II.b, II.c, II.d, II.e, II.f; the three other siblings of the eight are not described), Family B (III.A, III.E, III.F, IV.B, IV.D, IV.F, V.B, V.C, V.D, VI.A), Family C (I.1, I.2, II.1, III.1; II.1's seven unaffected siblings and two other daughters not described individually), plus previously published people in the Discussion with individual facts: Namekawa^18 two brothers, Shiihara^20 boy, sister and mother, Stumpf^21 juvenile-onset individual and 30-year-old female. Namekawa brothers' untested, unaffected parents were left out. Tested-negative relatives (II.b, I.b, V.C, I.1, I.2) have individual rows but no variant rows. Labels of Families A (II.c), B (III.F) and C (II.1) do not collide, so no '(Family n)' suffix. cDNA strings are printed without 'c.' (e.g. '739T→C'); recorded verbatim in cdna_hgvs_as_stated. No transcript or variant class is printed for any variant. Onset ages: 'presented at X' was used as onset for II.d, VI.A and III.F; II.c's onset given as text only (presented at 26 with a 1-year history), no ISO. Inheritance in Family A recorded as inherited paternal because the father's testicular DNA was heterozygous for p.Ser247Pro, although the Discussion says germline mosaicism cannot be excluded. source_reference_in_review filled for II.c and II.d (Duckett et al.^3), III.F (Seil et al.^2) and IV.B/IV.D/IV.F (Schwankhaus et al.^8), which are re-reports of earlier patients with new data. Contradictions: (1) I.a died 'at the age of 66' (Results) but 'lived until 62' (Discussion); deceased age left null. (2) Family C is 'three generations' in the text but 'Two generation family' in the Figure 1 legend. (3) The reference is spelled 'Schwankaus' and 'Schwankhaus'. Normal findings recorded as exclusions per D-27: 'remains cognitively intact' (II.d) and 'above-average intelligence' (VI.A) as cognitive impairment excluded. Head circumferences 59.5 cm (98%) for II.d and 58 cm (98%) for II.f are not called macrocephaly by the paper; no row and macrocephaly checklist left not reported. III.1's cause of death is not stated (found unresponsive with blood alcohol 0.22%); left not reported. V.B, V.D and III.1 zygosity not stated ('same mutation'); left not reported. Family-level 'no neurological symptoms' statements were not used to exclude specific checklist items. No stacked cells in this paper.
